title: Flagpost module manifest (v2)
description: The plugin.yaml manifest that describes a Flagpost artifact — a content pack (Tier 0) or a module (Tier 1 declarative / Tier 2 code). Draft: ADR-0040, docs/MODULES.md §4. Backwards-compatible with the v1 required-core manifests (which omit manifest_version, publisher, and trust_tier and are treated as first-party kernel-trusted code).

manifest_version.description: 2 for this schema. Absent/1 = a legacy first-party manifest (the in-box required-core modules); third-party artifacts MUST declare 2.

id.description: Stable, globally-unique module identifier. Lowercase; the directory name under backend/plugins/ for in-box modules. Third-party ids SHOULD be namespaced (publisher.name) to avoid collisions.

kind.description: pack = data-only content (Tier 0), consumed by the content-import path. module = executable feature (Tier 1/2), consumed by the plugin loader.

publisher.description: Who authored the artifact. Optional for in-box first-party modules; REQUIRED for anything distributed through a registry.

requires_flagpost.description: Platform compatibility. flagpost_min is inclusive; flagpost_max is exclusive. The instance refuses to install/load an artifact outside this range.

dependencies.description: Ids of other modules that must be present and enabled before this one loads (enforced topologically by the loader). Packs take no dependencies.

pack.description: Present only when kind = pack. Describes the data payload.

required_core.description: In-box only: this module is part of the required-core floor and carries no per-competition toggle (§11.3). A registry-distributed module is never required_core.

trust_tier.description: Present only when kind = module. declarative = config + server-driven UI, no arbitrary backend code (Tier 1). code = ships backend code that runs in-process (Tier 2). sandboxed is RESERVED for the deferred isolation story (Tier 3, ARCHITECTURE §15) and MUST NOT be used yet.

provides.description: Coarse declaration of what a module wires. Used by the loader and shown (as capabilities) on the install confirmation screen.

capabilities.description: The capability grants a module requests. Every entry is surfaced on the confirmation screen for explicit operator consent and recorded in the install audit. A declarative module may request only the declarative-safe subset (no network.egress / migrations.run / permissions.define).

permissions.description: RBAC permissions this module defines (code tier only). On install they are registered into the permission catalog so Administrators receive them without a hand-written migration; on uninstall they are retired. Mirrors the shape of auth/permissions.py.

settings.description: Declarative settings schema the module contributes. The admin settings UI renders a form from this and persists values through a generic per-module store — no bespoke router per module.

nav_items.description: Navigation entries the module contributes, surfaced through the existing is_module_enabled gating instead of a hardcoded nav list.

widgets.description: Dashboard widgets the module contributes, described declaratively and rendered by the existing dashboard-grid registry (§11.2).

extensions.description: Contributions into named frontend extension slots (§11.2), keyed by slot name (e.g. challenge.tabs, dashboard.widgets, team.detail.panels).

data_source.description: A read route the widget renders from. Must be a route the contributing module provides.

component.description: A component id the compiled frontend registry knows how to render for this slot. NOT arbitrary markup or code.

target.description: Where the pack installs. challenges + automation-recipes install into a competition (scoped); theme + translations are site-wide.
